entries.name: Olive
entries.voxel_shape: gnarled twisted trunk, rounded silvery crown
entries.notes: The Mediterranean in one tree; a single gnarled ancient can anchor a village square or hillside. Slow, near-immortal, and the default landmark of any coastal plain.

entries.name: Holm oak
entries.leaves: evergreen, dark glossy, spiny-edged when young
entries.fruit: acorn, ripens in the second autumn
entries.voxel_shape: broad dense evergreen crown, stout trunk
entries.notes: The evergreen oak that holds the maquis together; acorns fatten pigs and game, so oaks pair naturally with open grazing (dehesa).

entries.name: Cork oak
entries.voxel_shape: thick fissured corky trunk, rounded crown
entries.notes: Harvested every 9-12 years without felling; the tree wears its own fireproof armour. A cork forest reads as a patchwork of stripped rust and unstripped grey.

entries.name: Italian stone pine
entries.fruit: large woody pine cone (pine nuts), ripens in the third year
entries.fire: survives (thick bark, high crown); cones open in heat
entries.voxel_shape: broad flat umbrella canopy high on a bare trunk
entries.notes: The umbrella silhouette of the coastal plain from Cadiz to Cyprus; cones litter the ground with pine nuts a forager can pick up.

entries.name: Italian cypress
entries.voxel_shape: narrow dark column, flame-shaped
entries.notes: The Tuscan column: windbreaks and cemetery lines for miles. Far too flammable to cluster near any camp.

entries.name: Aleppo pine
entries.leaves: evergreen needles in pairs, light green
entries.fruit: small reddish cones, serotinous (open after fire)
entries.fire: killed; serotinous cones open after fire
entries.voxel_shape: irregular open crown, often leaning
entries.notes: The fire-follower pine; cones pop open in heat so it carpets freshly burnt hillsides first. A marker that a slope has burned recently.

entries.name: Carob
entries.fruit: flat dark pod (locust bean) 10-30 cm, sweet pulp
entries.voxel_shape: thick gnarled trunk, broad spreading crown
entries.notes: The drought-proof orchard tree; carob pods were the original sweetener. The carob seed gave the carat its weight — big gnarled giants make landmarks.

entries.name: Fig
entries.fruit: syconium (the fig), June and Aug-Oct crops
entries.voxel_shape: broad low dome on knuckled stems, milky latex
entries.notes: First fruit of the warm season; two crops a year in hot sites. Figs escape and naturalize along walls, ruins and streambeds.

entries.name: Pomegranate
entries.fruit: leathery crowned berry packed with red arils
entries.voxel_shape: rounded thorny multi-stem shrub, red bells then jewelled fruit
entries.notes: Native to Iran and the Caucasus, ancient in Mediterranean gardens; the classic dry-garden fruit and a dye source for leather and wool.

entries.name: Almond
entries.flowers: white to pink, very early spring, before the leaves
entries.fruit: downy hull over a pitted shell with the kernel
entries.voxel_shape: small spreading grey tree, cloud of pink-white blossom
entries.notes: Blossoms months before anything else; bare grey wood detonates into pink-white in February — the first colour of the Mediterranean spring.

entries.name: Strawberry tree
entries.fruit: red warty berry ('tree strawberry'), fruit and blossom together
entries.voxel_shape: twisted trunk, red flaking bark, round crown with red fruit
entries.notes: Fruit and blossom on the same branch in October; the seville liqueur tree and a classic post-fire resprouter of recovering slopes.

entries.name: Bay laurel
entries.voxel_shape: small dense dark pyramid or dome, glossy leaves
entries.notes: Apollo's laurel; dark shining thickets you smell before you see. One bay leaf per stew — crushed, it's the whole kitchen.

entries.name: Sweet chestnut
entries.flowers: upright yellow catkins, strongly scented, early summer
entries.voxel_shape: massive trunk, broad toothed dome
entries.notes: The mountain breadbasket of Italy and southern France; ancient giants over a thousand years old. Needs deep, cool, moist soils — not the dry lowlands.

entries.name: Pubescent oak
entries.voxel_shape: squat gnarled oak, downy grey leaves
entries.notes: The droughtiest of the oaks; squat, grey, toothed leaves that shrug off summer. Coppice for fuel and pigs.

entries.name: Judas tree
entries.flowers: magenta-pink clusters directly on the bare bark, early spring
entries.voxel_shape: small rounded tree, flower-studded bare trunk in spring
entries.notes: Cauliflory: flowers stapled onto naked bark in April; one blooming Judas stops traffic. Named for the legend of Judas Iscariot's hanging.

entries.name: Mediterranean fan palm
entries.voxel_shape: clump of thick fans on short fibrous stems
entries.notes: Europe's only native palm; blue-green fans that laugh off frost and drought. Sharp-toothed leaf stalks — keep the player's hands honest.

entries.name: Terebinth
entries.voxel_shape: small gnarled tree; crush a leaf for turpentine smell
entries.notes: The stinkier cousin of the pistachio; its galls fed the red and black dyes of antiquity, and its resin was a true turpentine.

entries.name: Grapevine
entries.fire: resprouts from old wood or base
entries.voxel_shape: climbing vine with curling tendrils
entries.notes: Wild lianas drape riparian thickets; the cultivated line runs the whole economy of the basin. Old vines twist into living sculpture.

entries.name: Rosemary
entries.flowers: pale blue, late winter to spring
entries.voxel_shape: needle bush leaking blue flowers and resin smell
entries.notes: The garrigue's own perfume; every step on limestone releases it. Bees make a pale, strong honey from its flowers.

entries.name: Thyme
entries.voxel_shape: low aromatic dome over bare rock
entries.notes: Low carpets of pink over bare rock in August; crush and the whole hillside smells of Provence. A field guide to dry limestone.

entries.name: Sage
entries.voxel_shape: grey felted mound with purple spikes
entries.notes: Dalmatian and Anatolian limestones; the felt-grey kitchen leaf for roast pork, brown butter and sausages.

entries.name: Stoechas lavender
entries.flowers: violet spike with upright 'rabbit ear' bracts, spring
entries.voxel_shape: grey bush with rabbit-ear purple spikes
entries.notes: The wild lavender of the western basin; a violet blaze after spring rain, gone resinous and oil-heavy by August.

entries.name: Myrtle
entries.voxel_shape: dense rounded aromatic shrub, white firework flowers
entries.notes: Sacred to Aphrodite; Roman bridal crowns. Berries go into myrtle liqueur, leaves onto roast pork and game in Sardinia.

entries.name: Lentisk (mastic)
entries.voxel_shape: dense dark glossy bush, low and spreading
entries.notes: Chewed in Chios for 2,500 years; the 'tears of Chios' are the original chewing gum and a prized spice in Greek sweets.

entries.name: Gum cistus (gum rockrose)
entries.flowers: large white, maroon blotch at the base, spring
entries.voxel_shape: sticky white-flowered dome with maroon blotches
entries.notes: The fire-follower; white blotched domes race each other over freshly burnt ground. Resinous and sweet — and a match-thrower in August.

entries.name: Spanish broom
entries.voxel_shape: fountain of canes loaded with yellow pea flowers
entries.notes: A fountain of green canes and June perfume; colonises roadcuts and bare ground. Its fibre was the original rope and broom.

entries.name: Oleander
entries.leaves: evergreen, in whorls of three, leathery
entries.voxel_shape: tall dark shrub in a dry torrent bed, pink blooms
entries.notes: Holds every dry torrent bed in bloom through August — but ALL parts kill: smoke, nectar, skewers, everything. A quiz-question plant for any camper.

entries.name: Kermes oak
entries.voxel_shape: impenetrable spiny evergreen thicket
entries.notes: The spiny thicket no goat wants; the kermes scale insects feeding on it produced the scarlet of cardinals and illuminated manuscripts.

entries.name: Tree heath
entries.voxel_shape: white-canopied heath on slopes
entries.notes: White honey-bells over Corsica and the Rif; the dense red burls at its roots are what pipe-makers prize, decades in the making.

entries.name: Caper
entries.leaves: deciduous, rounded, fleshy, with spiny stipules
entries.voxel_shape: sprawling wall shrub with big white star-flowers
entries.notes: Grows out of rock cracks and old mortar; buds picked one by one before they open. The culinary definition of 'thriving on neglect'.

entries.name: Giant reed
entries.leaves: long canes with blade leaves; canes survive winter
entries.flowers: large silky panicle, late summer to autumn
entries.fruit: seeds mostly sterile; spreads by rhizomes
entries.voxel_shape: bamboo-like cane thicket with feathery plume
entries.notes: The bamboo of the Mediterranean; canes became roofs, fishing rods and clarinet reeds — and it chokes every waterway it can reach.

entries.name: Asphodel
entries.flowers: white star-flowers on a branched spike, spring
entries.voxel_shape: branched spike of white stars over dry grass
entries.notes: Homer's 'fields of asphodel'; dense white star-spikes carpet tired, overgrazed pastures. Neither grazed nor loved — an underworld plant.

entries.name: Sea fennel (rock samphire)
entries.voxel_shape: grey succulent cushion on coastal rocks
entries.notes: The original samphire; fleshy leaves pickled in every port since antiquity. Brutally salty crunch on the rock pools — poor man's asparagus.

entries.name: Ivy-leaved cyclamen
entries.leaves: heart-shaped, marbled silver, grows from autumn
entries.flowers: swept-back pink petals, autumn, before leaves or after they fall
entries.voxel_shape: pink shooting stars under oaks
entries.notes: Pink swept-back stars on bare autumn ground under holm oaks; the tuber is toxic (saponins), the flower beloved ground cover.

entries.name: Bee orchid
entries.flowers: velvety bee-mimicking lip, late spring; mostly self-pollinating
entries.voxel_shape: thin spike; flowers faking a female bee
entries.notes: Flowers so like a female bee that males attempt mating with them; among the wildest bets in European evolution — and still mostly self-pollinates.

entries.name: Prickly pear
entries.fruit: oval tuna, orange-red, covered in glochids
entries.voxel_shape: paddle-stacked cactus, orange fruit on top
entries.notes: Across the Mediterranean since Columbus; pads and tuna fruit feed people, cochineal beetles and goats. Frost-killed below -7 C, but resprouts hard.

entries.name: Saffron milk cap
entries.fruit: orange cap bruising green, carrot-red latex
entries.voxel_shape: orange cap bruising blue-green, under pines
entries.notes: The Catalan rovello and Valencian esclata-sang; grilled with garlic or salt-and-jar, it is autumn's best edible. Height here is the fruitbody (cap) size.

entries.name: Death cap
entries.fruit: greenish cap, white gills, ring and volva
entries.voxel_shape: pale green-white mushroom with skirt and sac at the base
entries.notes: Half of all mushroom fatalities; pleasant smell, innocent cap, fulminant liver failure days later. Grows under oaks and chestnuts — teach the player to walk past.

entries.name: Bronze bolete (cep)
entries.fruit: dark brown cap, pale pores, stout stem
entries.voxel_shape: dark brown cap on a stout pale stem, under oaks
entries.notes: The 'cep de Bordeaux'; summer oak and chestnut country. Dries beautifully and is worth real coin — good foraging loot. Height is the fruitbody.
